hypothesis_queue.physical_signature: Cross-catchment replication of signed channel-profile breaks, normalized within catchment and channel-order strata and tested against a slope-matched pseudo-crest null.
hypothesis_queue.missing_fault_rationale: A blind or unmapped rupture can perturb channel profiles and low-relief surfaces across several independent catchments without producing a single catalogue-grade scarp; repeated, strike-compatible breaks are the proposed discriminator.
hypothesis_queue.non_fault_mimic: Lithologic knickzones, inherited drainage capture, and regional base-level or climate change can also produce channel-profile breaks.
hypothesis_queue.difference_from_repo: QTSK/TDKL score local knickwave magnitude or scarp polarity. FARC requires cross-catchment replication against a channel-order/slope-matched null; no matching implementation or experiment card was found in this repository.
hypothesis_queue.external_data: none proposed; uses existing DEM-derived cached channels. The restored owner mirror is not authenticated against current organizer files.

hypothesis_queue.physical_signature: A depth-conditioned temperature-to-conductivity residual: retain local thermal anomalies not explained by regional conductance or basin depth, then test spatial coherence along blind structures.
hypothesis_queue.missing_fault_rationale: Focused fluid flow could make a thermal/conductivity residual near a buried fault even where the surface scarp is absent; this tests a geothermal-fluid association rather than treating a vent as a fault label.
hypothesis_queue.non_fault_mimic: Lake-brine conductivity, groundwater circulation, and unfractured permeable lithology can produce the same thermal/conductive anomaly.
hypothesis_queue.difference_from_repo: DHTC combines deep heat/MT and basement structure; TCONS would use head-/depth-matched negative controls to isolate the conditional residual. No exact TCONS method was found in the repository.
hypothesis_queue.external_data: none proposed beyond the cached stack; before sharing derivatives, verify the official DOE GDR INGENIOUS source and license at https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391. Current owner-mirror provenance is not independently authenticated.

hypothesis_queue.physical_signature: A terrain-bin-matched K:Th radiometric residual with along-strike persistence, rather than a global radiometric high.
hypothesis_queue.missing_fault_rationale: Hydrothermal alteration or soil redistribution along a covered structure may persist in shallow radiometry even where no discrete scarp was mapped; terrain matching is intended to remove relief-related baseline effects.
hypothesis_queue.non_fault_mimic: K-rich transported alluvium, parent-rock boundaries, and soil-moisture effects can produce the same K:Th contrast.
hypothesis_queue.difference_from_repo: MVRD uses radiometric evidence with scarp fields; PRAN proposes a terrain-conditioned null and along-strike persistence rather than catalogue-derived placement. No exact PRAN experiment was found in the repository.
hypothesis_queue.external_data: none proposed; uses cached GeoDAWN-derived radiometry and existing terrain layers. The owner-mirror values and redistribution terms still require verification.

hypothesis_queue.physical_signature: Cross-sensor edge persistence after a predeclared survey-line-direction artifact veto and local continuity test.
hypothesis_queue.missing_fault_rationale: A real concealed structure should be supported by independent sensors and should not exist only as an acquisition-direction seam; this is a robustness-oriented detector for faults lacking obvious surface expression.
hypothesis_queue.non_fault_mimic: Tie-line leveling, gridding artifacts, and broad lithologic contacts aligned with acquisition direction can mimic the signature.
hypothesis_queue.difference_from_repo: MGC/XGCE compare cross-field edge geometry but do not use this explicit flight-direction null; FLAC is a quality-controlled edge persistence test. No exact FLAC experiment was found in the repository.
hypothesis_queue.external_data: none proposed; GeoDAWN acquisition metadata is an official manual-review source, not a new raster. The current run did not re-fetch that source.
